decision_nodes.title: Psych Triage
decision_nodes.body:
**What is the PRIMARY presenting concern?**

Select the most urgent/dominant feature. Many psychiatric presentations overlap — this routes to the most appropriate starting point.

options.label: Agitation / Aggression
options.description: Combative, threatening, pacing, unable to cooperate

options.label: Withdrawal Symptoms
options.description: Tremor, diaphoresis, tachycardia, h/o alcohol/benzo/opioid use

options.label: Unresponsive / Mute / Rigid
options.description: Catatonic features, not speaking, waxy flexibility

options.label: Not Eating / Purging
options.description: Eating disorder presentation, weight loss, electrolyte concerns

decision_nodes.summary: Route to appropriate psychiatric pathway based on primary presenting concern.

decision_nodes.title: Agitation Pathway
decision_nodes.body:
**→ [Acute Agitation Consult](#/tree/acute-agitation)**

**Immediate priorities:**
• Verbal de-escalation (BETA protocol)
• Chemical restraint if de-escalation fails
• Rule out organic causes (hypoglycemia, hypoxia, intoxication)

**Key decision:** Is this delirium/medical OR primary psychiatric?
decision_nodes.summary: Agitated patient — route to Acute Agitation consult for BETA protocol and chemical restraint.

decision_nodes.title: Suicidal Patient Pathway
decision_nodes.body:
**→ [Suicidal Patient Consult](#/tree/suicidal-patient)**

**Immediate priorities:**
• 1:1 constant visual observation
• Remove ligatures, sharps, medications from room
• Environmental safety checklist
• ASQ or C-SSRS screening

**Key decision:** Risk stratification → disposition (discharge vs voluntary vs involuntary)
decision_nodes.summary: Suicidal patient — route to Suicidal Patient consult for C-SSRS and risk stratification.

decision_nodes.title: Altered Mental Status Pathway
decision_nodes.body:
**→ [Medical Clearance - Psych](#/tree/medical-clearance-psych)**

**Critical question:** Is this DELIRIUM or PRIMARY PSYCHOSIS?

**Delirium red flags:**
• Acute onset (hours-days)
• Fluctuating course
• Inattention (cannot focus on interview)
• Visual hallucinations
• Abnormal vital signs
• Age >45 with first psychiatric symptoms

**20% of acute psychosis has a medical etiology.** Always rule out organic causes first.
decision_nodes.summary: Altered mental status — route to Medical Clearance for organic workup.

decision_nodes.title: Psychosis Pathway
decision_nodes.body:
**Start with:** [Medical Clearance - Psych](#/tree/medical-clearance-psych)

**Rule out organic causes FIRST:**
• Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis
• Stimulant intoxication
• Medication toxicity
• Encephalitis/meningitis
• Metabolic derangement

**New-onset psychosis in patient >45:** Medical cause until proven otherwise.

**If agitated:** [Acute Agitation](#/tree/acute-agitation) for chemical restraint options.
decision_nodes.summary: Psychosis — start with medical clearance to rule out organic causes.

decision_nodes.title: Anxiety / Panic Pathway
decision_nodes.body:
**Panic attack vs medical emergency:**

Before diagnosing panic, rule out:
• Pulmonary embolism (consider PERC, Wells)
• Acute coronary syndrome (especially if risk factors)
• Arrhythmia (check ECG)
• Hyperthyroidism
• Pheochromocytoma
• Stimulant intoxication

**If true panic attack:**
• Reassurance, calm environment
• Breathing exercises
• Benzodiazepine if severe (lorazepam 0.5-1 mg PO/SL)
• Outpatient psychiatry/therapy referral
decision_nodes.summary: Anxiety/panic — rule out PE, ACS, arrhythmia before diagnosing panic disorder.

decision_nodes.title: Withdrawal Pathway
decision_nodes.body:
**→ [Alcohol Withdrawal Consult](#/tree/alcohol-withdrawal)**

**Early treatment prevents:**
• Withdrawal seizures (peak 12-48h)
• Delirium tremens (peak 48-96h, mortality 5-15%)

**Which substance?**
• **Alcohol/Benzos:** CIWA-Ar, benzodiazepines, phenobarbital
• **Opioids:** COWS score, buprenorphine initiation, clonidine
• **Stimulants:** Supportive care, benzos for agitation

**High-risk features:** Prior seizures/DTs, PAWSS ≥4, prolonged heavy use
decision_nodes.summary: Withdrawal — route to Alcohol Withdrawal consult for CIWA-Ar and benzo protocols.

decision_nodes.title: Catatonia Pathway
decision_nodes.body:
**Recognize catatonia early — it's treatable!**

**Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale:**
• Immobility / stupor
• Mutism
• Staring / fixed gaze
• Posturing / waxy flexibility
• Negativism (resistance to movement)

**Treatment:**
• **Lorazepam challenge:** 2 mg IV — improvement within 10 min confirms diagnosis
• If response: Continue lorazepam 2 mg q4-6h
• If no response: Consider ECT

⚠️ **AVOID antipsychotics initially** — can trigger malignant catatonia or NMS
decision_nodes.summary: Catatonia — lorazepam challenge 2 mg IV. Avoid antipsychotics initially.

decision_nodes.title: Medication Reaction Pathway
decision_nodes.body:
**Differentiate these emergencies:**

| Feature | NMS | Serotonin Syndrome | Dystonia |
|---------|-----|-------------------|----------|
| **Onset** | Days | Hours | Minutes-hours |
| **Rigidity** | Lead-pipe | Hyperreflexia, clonus | Focal (torticollis, oculogyric) |
| **Temp** | >40°C | Variable | Normal |
| **Mental status** | Altered | Agitated | Clear |
| **Pupils** | Normal | Dilated | Normal |
| **Cause** | Antipsychotics | SSRIs, MAOIs | Antipsychotics, antiemetics |

**Treatments:**
• **NMS:** Stop offending agent, dantrolene, bromocriptine, cooling
• **Serotonin syndrome:** Stop offending agent, cyproheptadine, benzos
• **Dystonia:** [Diphenhydramine](#/drug/diphenhydramine/dystonia) 50 mg IV/IM or benztropine 2 mg
decision_nodes.summary: Med reaction — differentiate NMS vs serotonin syndrome vs dystonia. Treatment differs.

decision_nodes.title: Eating Disorder Pathway
decision_nodes.body:
**Eating disorder emergency — focus on medical stability:**

**Check immediately:**
• Electrolytes: K+, PO4, Mg2+ (refeeding risk)
• ECG: QTc prolongation, bradycardia
• Glucose
• Vitals: Bradycardia, orthostatic hypotension

**MARSIPAN criteria for admission:**
• BMI <13 or rapid weight loss >1 kg/week
• K+ <3.0 or PO4 <0.5
• HR <40 or BP <90 systolic
• QTc >450 ms
• Syncope
• Hypoglycemia

**Refeeding syndrome risk:** Start feeding slowly, monitor PO4/K+/Mg2+ daily × 3 days
decision_nodes.summary: Eating disorder — check electrolytes, ECG, vitals. Refeeding syndrome risk.

decision_nodes.title: Routed to Consult
decision_nodes.body:
Continue with the linked specialty consult for detailed management.

**Return to Psych Triage** if the clinical picture changes or a different pathway is needed.
decision_nodes.recommendation: Follow the linked consult pathway for detailed management.
decision_nodes.summary: Continue with specialty consult for detailed management.
